text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Thursday, traders said.
Gas oil was virtually unchanged in a quietish market.
With regards to Russian material buyers and sellers appeared to be wide apart with premiums assessed at around quotes cif hi +$1.00/+$2.50 basis Genoa.
A Swiss-based trader was reported to have two Russian cargoes on offer and the market was waiting for the dates on a slew of end June, early July cargoes.
Turkey was reported to have tendered for one cargo of gas oil for end June, start July delivery with an optional cargo.
Low sulphur material was fairly firm with diffs assessed around quotes fob hi +$3.50/+$4.0.
Naphtha prices were steady to lower with cif cargoes basis Italy notionally valued at $180/$182 cif.

"In the Med there is not much interest left for June," a Spanish trader said. "Basically the market is more or less balanced...It is true there are not many cargoes but there is not a big rush for demand either."
Cargoes slipped after NWE pulled back from a deal yesterday at $186.75 cif basis Rotterdam for an Egyptian Alex cargo. Offers were heard in NWE at $185 for Dow spec and Algerian.
Gasoline was steady to lower. Traders said prices were still supported by the recent Turkish tender and snug premium unleaded supplies.
Traders were mixed about high sulphur fuel oil with some saying it was steady at the $76/$79 a tonne fob mark with supply a little tight but with demand thin as well.
Others said there were some signs of weakness with high sulphur barges in the north not holding their recent higher levels.
"The (Med) market is pretty weak as barges in the north are getting a little weaker; they are not holding the trend set earlier at $87/$88 fob. I also don't see that much demand," one trader said.
An Italian refiner said it picked up a high sulphur M-100 cargo at high cif plus $3 or $4 on Wednesday from a French refiner.
The French refiner was re-offering a high sulphur cargo it picked up at $83 fob earlier this week on a delivered basis with a price tag of high cif plus $3.50/$4.

A low quality high sulphur M-100 out of Russia's Black Sea Novorossiisk oil terminal was heard on the water, but no further details were available. Traders said no immediate buyers were seen for that one.
